inputs.text: This ruling looks less like a straightforward religious-freedom dispute and more like a carefully chosen way to make abortion limits politically untouchable. The ACLU and Hoosier Jews for Choice argued that the Indiana law burdened abortion access tied to sincerely held beliefs, and now the fight can be recast as the state attacking faith. LifeNews.com’s inflammatory title pushes the opposite framing, but both sides’ messaging helps turn a contested policy into a battle over religious identity—exactly the kind of framing that shields the underlying agenda from scrutiny.
